## Findings
- claim-1: Conditional on task 67’s five boundary-aware matrices, unimodular complementary minors retaining \(H=s_{(i^j,3)}\) exist in every regime \(i,j\ge3\), \(p,c\ge1\), \(\min(p,c)=1\). Thus no first failure occurs.
## Strategy
For each of task 67’s five regimes, retain \(H\) and delete its column from the stated \(R_{\mathrm{selected}}\). The resulting complementary minors are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
(p,c)&\text{selected rows}&\text{complementary columns}&\det\\ \hline
(1,1)&(r_1,r_2,r_5)&(C,E,F)&-1\\
(1,2)&(r_1,r_2,r_5,r_6,r_8)&(C,E,F,G,I)&-1\\
(1,\ge3)&(r_1,r_2,r_5,r_6,r_7,r_8)&(C,E,F,G,I,J)&-1\\
(2,1)&(r_1,r_4,r_5,r_6,r_7)&(B,C,D,E,F)&1\\
(\ge3,1)&(r_1,r_3,r_4,r_5,r_6,r_7)&(A,B,C,D,E,F)&1
\end{array}
\]

These are unimodular. Since task 67 gives
\(R_{\mathrm{full}}=\mathcal C R_{\mathrm{selected}}\), the selected rows generate the full Pieri row lattice integrally in each regime. Thus projection to the displayed non-\(H\) columns is unimodular, while \(H=s_{(i^j,3)}\) is retained.

The five regimes exhaust \(p,c\ge1\) with \(\min(p,c)=1\). Therefore the requested conditional degree-\(d+3\) target is established: no failure occurs among these regimes.

## Gaps
This uses task 67’s conditional box/Schur/Pieri presentation and applies only for its hypotheses \(i,j\ge3\) and \(\min(p,c)=1\). It gives no conclusion in other boundary ranges or in higher degrees.

## Next
A separate calculation is required for regimes outside task 67 or for degrees beyond \(d+3\).
